summary: Read the dispatch, lean-egf/docs/CAMPAIGN.md, kb 0001/0006/0015, the roadmap block of papers/egf/programme/roadmap.toml, corrections C-1..C-6 and C-35, the ledger and curation rows of cor:pinsker_negative_control, main.tex:300-340, 360-425 and 728-752, the strict definitions Loss.lean relies on (EGF/Defs.lean, Sampling.lean, SamplingCorollaries.lean, BackwardPolicy.lean), and all 1356 lines of Loss.lean, against every label and finding of REPORT.json. Reran the typecheck. Ran #print axioms on all 83 declarations the REPORT names, from a copy under the campaign directory, now deleted. The statements are faithful, the refutation instances meet every presupposition, and the numbers check by hand. No unearned mark, no sorry, standard axioms, scope clean. labels.label: cor:pinsker_negative_control
labels.notes: Not marked here (the head-4000 regex of tools/ledger.py finds no mark; the label line `cor:pinsker_negative_control` — `main.tex:374` is at character 151). That is correct: the label is marked in EGF/SamplingCorollaries.lean in its corrected form of record (DEC-141, C-1), and the REPORT row is 'partial'. (1) EGF.klwfmLoss equals Eq. (15) (l.363-366) with the corrected deltaFinitDensity = max(0, -(f_init + f_in - f_out)) on the penalty and ftermHatDensity in the cross-entropy. The value top off LossFinite is the paper's value whenever b > 0 and H(kappa) is finite. Case by case: kappa charging {f-hat = 0} gives -E log f-hat = +inf, because crossEntropy_posPart_integrable makes max(log f-hat, 0) kappa-integrable; log f-hat not in L1(kappa) has an infinite negative part, so the cross-entropy is +inf; the penalty integrand is measurable and >= 0, so non-integrability means E_nu = +inf, times b > 0. Every theorem carries hent, and every theorem forces b > 0: N = 0 with lam <= 0 . nu_train gives lam = 0, which contradicts kappa << lam for a probability kappa. Reading nu_train as a measure on states does not narrow the statement. Every theorem quantifies over all nu_train. A path distribution enters Eq. (15) only through the state integral of delta f_init, i.e. through a (weighted) occupation measure on states, which is such a measure. The paper itself takes nu_train 'the uniform distribution on the vertices' at main.tex:338. For a probability, E_{s~nu_train} is the integral; the l.159 normalization of an unnormalized measure only rescales b. The question is disclosed. (2) EGF.kl_decomposition is l.418-420 in the direction KL(kappa || kappa-hat/kappa-hat(S)), with Mathlib's klDiv between two probabilities, so the mass correction vanishes. Its hypotheses kappa << kappa-hat and hce are not restrictions in (-inf, +inf]: klDiv_eq_top_iff_crossEntropy covers the +inf case. Hand check of Null.printed_kl_decomposition_false_finite (Bool, counting measure, policy id, F_out = 0, so kappa-hat = F_init = uniform; kappa = q = 1/4 delta_true + 3/4 delta_false): KL(q || unif) = 1/4 log(1/2) + 3/4 log(3/2) = 3/4 log 3 - log 2, and the printed right side is log 2 + 0 - (2 log 2 - 3/4 log 3), the same value. KL(unif || q) = 1/2 log 2 + 1/2 log(2/3) = log 2 - 1/2 log 3. They are equal iff 3^5 = 2^8 (243 vs 256), so they differ. The instance meets every presupposition: F_init(S) = 1, kappa a probability << lambda, finite entropy, finite cross-entropy, a valid generative flow. Using a second kl_decomposition with F_init := q only to evaluate klDiv unif q is legitimate. Null.printed_kl_decomposition_false (kappa = delta_true, left side +inf against a finite right side) and printed_kl_decomposition_false_of_not_ac are correct, and KLDecompositionPrinted is a faithful Prop of the printed identity on these finite instances. pinsker_negative_control_rev, _density_rev and _min need only F_init and kappa probabilities (measure form) or the paper's density presuppositions, and follow from sampling_error_control, tvDist_comm and pinsker. (3) loss_sub_entropy_ge holds for every b: L - H = KL - log(1 + delta) + b E_nu delta f >= KL + (b - N) E_nu delta f, using log(1 + x) <= x and delta <= N E_nu delta f. So b >= N suffices for loss_ge_entropy, and b >= 1 + N gives loss_controls_defect and loss_controls_sampling (delta/(1 + delta) <= min(1, delta) <= min(1, N(L - H))). Every hypothesis is named: hinit, hout, hin (or hPhi for the _nonsingular forms), hkappa, hent, hN, hb, hL. Not vacuous: Null.loss_controls_sampling_inhabited (delta = 0, b = 2, N = 1) and SwapM.lossFinite (delta = m > 0). SwapM checked by hand: inflow = m delta_true, f-hat(true) = 1 + m, delta f(false) = m, H(delta_true) = 0, L = b m - log(1 + m), printed L = -b m - log(1 + m), which tends to -inf as m -> inf for b >= 0. loss_lt_entropy at m = 1: b - log 2 < 0 for b < log 2. (4) The l.400 finding: see findings. Every proved statement is true. reverse_isFlowMatching_iff: F_in B = F_out for a backward policy, and kappa-hat + F_out = F_init + delta F_init + F_in, which is the virtual flow of def:virtual_flows, l.316. reverse_cont_ae_eq and printed_reverse_not_isFlowMatching hold for every Markov B: masses 1 + delta against delta. algBackwardFactorReversed_eq gives the comparison where f_in > 0: equality iff f_init = 0. (5) algBackwardFactor_mem_Ioc is correct. Swap3 checked: inflow{false} = 1, F_out{false} = 3, f_init(false) = 0, defect -2, printed factor (1 - 2)^-1 = -1, corrected factor 1/3. cont_kappaHat_ae_eq_forwardFactor is the sampler's continuation f_out/(f-hat + f_out), (kappa-hat + F_out)-a.e., split where f_out = 0. (6) C-6 forms: InflowAC is discharged by EGF.InflowAC.of_map_ac / of_isEGF, and there is no Jacobian hypothesis.

findings.where: campaign/T-egf-loss/REPORT.json:242-259 (proposed correction 'new', kind 'false (under the time-reversal reading; see questions)'); scaffold/EGFScaffold/Loss.lean:1003-1005 (docstring of algBackwardFactorReversed_eq)
findings.what: The l.400 finding depends on a reading; it is not about what the paper prints as such. main.tex:392 says only that B_<- is filled 'using (kappa, pi_<-^*) ... with t in {1,...,tau}', and never says what law the backward paths, or their weights p_t, are meant to have. Eq. (15) accepts any nu_train, and the theorems hold for every nu_train with lam <= N nu_train. So the printed weight (1 + delta f_init/f_in)^-1 defines a legitimate backward weighting. It is not a wrong formula unless B_<- is meant to hold reversed-sampler paths. Proved, and true: the reversed flow (B, F_in) is flow matching from kappa-hat exactly to F_init + delta F_init, the virtual initial of def:virtual_flows, main.tex:316. Its sampler continues with (1 + (f_init + delta f_init)/f_in)^-1, while the printed factor is its continuation toward delta F_init alone, which is not flow matching. The two agree where f_in > 0 iff f_init = 0. Not proved, and disclosed in SCOPE (Loss.lean:61-62): that this sampler's path law is the time reversal of the forward sampler's paths. That identification is exact only for a flow-matching flow (delta = 0, or the forward chain started from the virtual initial F_init + delta F_init). For the actual forward sampler from F_init with delta > 0, its occupation measure differs from kappa-hat + F_out. The question at REPORT.json:150 ('time reversals of sampler paths, i.e. the reversed sampler from kappa') states the identification as if it held in general. The docstring sentence 'the printed weights overstate the survival of a backward path wherever the source has density' presumes the reading. The paper's notation supports the reading but does not settle it: the forward factor of l.399 uses f-hat_term, the density of the virtual terminal, so the backward analogue would be f-hat_init = f_init + delta f_init (l.316), and the printed delta f_init would then be missing f_init.
findings.fix: File this as an OQ row (DEC-141: readings stay OQ rows), not as a correction of kind 'false'. Word it: 'if B_<- holds reversed-sampler paths (the time reversal of the virtual forward sampler), the weight of l.400 omits f_init; the reversed flow (B, F_in) is flow matching from kappa-hat to F_init + delta F_init (EGF.reverse_isFlowMatching_iff) and continues with (1 + (f_init + delta f_init)/f_in)^-1 (EGF.reverse_cont_ae_eq_backwardFactor); the printed weight is the continuation toward delta F_init alone (EGF.printed_reverse_not_isFlowMatching); in a trained flow the printed weights are identically 1'. Add 'under that reading' to the docstring at Loss.lean:1004-1005, and drop the general 'i.e.' in the question. No change is needed to any proved statement.

findings.where: scaffold/EGFScaffold/Loss.lean:35 (checklist row b > 0); campaign/T-egf-loss/REPORT.json:99 (hypotheses row b > 0)
findings.what: 'the control needs b >= 1 + N' and 'the floor H <= L needs b >= N' claim necessity. Lean proves only sufficiency (loss_ge_entropy, loss_controls_defect, loss_controls_sampling) and a refutation at a single point: SwapM.loss_lt_entropy, b < log 2 at N = 1, m = 1. For the floor, b >= N is in fact necessary: in SwapM with nu_train = lam/N, L - H = (b/N) m - log(1 + m), which is < 0 for small m > 0 whenever b < N, because log(1 + m)/m -> 1. But this is not proved. For the control, necessity of b >= 1 + N is not known. C-35's corrected text ('b >= 1 + ||d lambda/d nu_train||_inf') is unaffected, since it is offered as a sufficient condition.
findings.fix: Write 'suffices' (or 'is proved for') instead of 'needs'. Or, cheaply, strengthen the refutation to: for every b < 1 there is m > 0 with L < H at N = 1 (choose m with b m < log(1 + m)). That makes 'the floor needs b >= N' a theorem at N = 1.

findings.what: 'the paper's +inf: klwfmLossReal where the loss is finite, top elsewhere' is stated without its conditions. top is the paper's value only when b > 0 and H(kappa) is finite: crossEntropy_posPart_integrable assumes hent. When the entropy is infinite the paper's value can be undefined or -inf; when b <= 0 and the penalty is not integrable it is -inf or undefined. No theorem is affected, since every theorem carries hent and forces b > 0. REPORT.json states the condition, but the definition's docstring does not.
findings.fix: Add 'for b > 0 and kappa of finite entropy (crossEntropy_posPart_integrable)' to the docstring of EGF.klwfmLoss.
